scope: Static review: no Rust toolchain on the audit machine
method: Detection only, reported raw. Nine auditors each read one area of the code against the leading tools and papers for that job. Seven cross-cutting auditors looked for what falls between areas: end-to-end data flow, benchmark integrity, scale, robustness, web security, the test suite, and language support. A second round then went file by file through each area to list everything the first round left out, with no cap on the count.

Three more agents researched what benchmark-grade evaluation means for this kind of tool, compared OpenHeart with competing engines and code-to-UML tools, and ran the automated checks that work without a Rust toolchain.

Findings were not verified before listing; each one cites the code it rests on so it can be checked while fixing. A few carry a note from a partial review that was stopped early. Findings marked disputed were challenged by that review.
Limits: cargo, clippy and the test suite could not be run on the audit machine, so no finding rests on a test run. Statements about runtime behavior come from reading the code.
